title: Designing a Better Command Palette
summary: This lesson covers the essential UX patterns for building a high-performance command palette (Cmd+K). It focuses on fuzzy matching, structured results, keyboard-only navigation, and handling async or empty states to empower power users.

transcript.text: Press command K. Type three letters. Jump anywhere.
It is not a search box. Type STG and it finds settings.
Fuzzy matching with the letters highlighted. Match the intent, not the string.
Never dump one flat list. Group results: recent first, then actions, then pages.
Structure is what makes it fast.
Your hands never touch the mouse. Arrows move. Enter runs. Escape closes.
A power user crosses the whole app blind.
Open it empty and most palettes show nothing. Show recent commands instead of a blank void.
Some commands fetch data before they run. Spin inline and keep the palette open.
Never freeze the whole screen for one call. Results load in place.
One command can open another. Change theme drills into its own sub-menu.
Escape walks you back one level, not all the way out.
Follow for more UI systems. Save this for your next command K.

on_screen_text: Match the intent, not the string.
design_principles: Fuzzy matching to match user intent over literal strings
Avoid blank voids by providing starting points in empty states
Non-blocking UI for asynchronous data fetching
before_after: Transforming a basic search box into a structured, keyboard-driven command palette with fuzzy matching and nested navigation.
